title: kate-syntax: Theme loader and Format-to-Style resolution
summary: Load KSyntaxHighlighting JSON themes (Breeze Light and Breeze Dark vendored, MIT) and resolve a Format against a Theme into a concrete Style: colors and font flags. Resolution order is the upstream one: per-definition custom styles in the theme, then the Format's own overrides, then the theme's default text style. Editor colors (background, current line, selection, line numbers) come along because the GUI needs them from the same file.

lane.reason: Small, mechanical, fully specified by two JSON files and a 30-entry enum. A good packet for a local open-weight model: the whole task fits in a 64k context and the test oracle is the upstream file itself.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: New module. Dependencies with justification: serde + serde_json (theme files are JSON; writing a JSON parser by hand would be the speculative abstraction).

regression_tests.name: theme::tests::breeze_light_and_dark_load
regression_tests.asserts: Both vendored themes parse; text_style(Keyword).fg equals the hex value in the JSON; editor_color(BackgroundColor) is present.

regression_tests.name: theme::tests::resolution_order_is_custom_then_format_then_default
regression_tests.asserts: With a custom style for (rust, Keyword), resolve uses it; without it a Format with italic=Some(true) yields italic over the default; a Format with no overrides yields the default exactly.

regression_tests.name: theme::tests::bad_color_is_an_error_not_black
regression_tests.asserts: A theme with '#GG0000' fails with ThemeError::BadColor naming the value.
